title: ATF4, ZIK1, and PNMA3 Transcriptomic Signatures Predict Chemoradiotherapy Response in Cervical Cancer.
authors: de Melo Neto, Angelo Borges; Queiroz, Fabio Ribeiro; de Souza Melo, Carolina Pereira; Duarte, Bruna Custodio Dias; Ferreira, Jorge Gomes Goulart; de Amorim, Izabela Ferreira Gontijo; do Amaral, Laurence Rodrigues; Bertarini, Pedro Luiz Lima; de Figueiredo Franco, Telma Maria Rossi; de Carvalho, Andrea Teixeira; Martins-Filho, Olindo Assis; de Jesus Jeremias, Wander; da Conceicao Braga, Leticia; de Oliveira Salles, Paulo Guilherme; de Souza Gomes, Matheus
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过RNA测序和机器学习识别宫颈癌放化疗反应相关的转录因子基因表达特征，但仅涉及基因表达统计，未进行蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与课题核心关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer (CC) is a main malignancy affecting women globally, with a high mortality rate. Chemoradiotherapy resistance is a significant factor in determining treatment outcomes, and prognostic biomarkers are essential for the appropriate selection of therapeutic strategies. This study aimed to identify gene expression signatures that may allow for follow-up treatment response in CC patients. METHODS: Samples of non-stem CC cells selected by Fluorescence-activated Cell Sorting from 21 Responders and 10 Non-responder patients, who attended the Mario Penna Institute (Belo Horizonte-Brazil) from August 2017 to May 2018, and submitted to Next-generation RNA sequencing, were analyzed to evaluate differential gene expression profiles between both groups. Machine Learning and statistical analyses were performed to identify a signature related to clinical outcomes. RESULTS: 2670 Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with log(2)FoldChange </= -1 or >/= 1 and adjusted p-value </= 0.05 were found. Of these, 1591 were protein-coding, but only 8 were considered relevant based on machine-learning and statistical analyses for classifying treatment response. However, only PNMA3 and ZIK1 were markedly upregulated in non-responder patients. Among the genes upregulated in Responder patients, only ATF4 and ATP1B3 were identified by machine-learning analysis. On the other hand, only ATF4, PNMA3, and ZIK1 were associated in network interactions, more specifically to apoptosis pathways, and the differential expression of ATF4 and PNMA3 occurred exclusively in cervical cancer non-stem cells, in the presence of ZIK1. CONCLUSIONS: We propose that upregulation of PNMA3 and downregulation of ATF4, specifically in cervical cancer non-stem cells, is associated with upregulation of ZIK1 and with resistance to apoptosis and chemoradiotherapy. Therefore, suggesting that these genes may serve as potential signatures for CC prognosis.
abstract_zh: 背景：宫颈癌（CC）是影响全球女性的主要恶性肿瘤，死亡率高。放化疗抵抗是决定治疗结果的重要因素，预后生物标志物对于适当选择治疗策略至关重要。本研究旨在识别可能用于宫颈癌患者后续治疗反应监测的基因表达特征。方法：通过荧光激活细胞分选（Fluorescence-activated Cell Sorting）从21名应答者和10名无应答者患者中选取非干细胞宫颈癌细胞样本，这些患者于2017年8月至2018年5月在Mario Penna研究所（巴西贝洛奥里藏特）就诊，并接受下一代RNA测序，分析两组间的差异基因表达谱。采用机器学习和统计分析来识别与临床结果相关的特征。结果：共发现2670个差异表达基因（DEGs），其log(2)倍数变化 ≤ -1 或 ≥ 1，且调整后p值 ≤ 0.05。其中，1591个为蛋白编码基因，但根据机器学习和统计分析，仅8个被认为与治疗反应分类相关。然而，只有PNMA3和ZIK1在无应答者患者中显著上调。在应答者患者中上调的基因中，仅ATF4和ATP1B3被机器学习分析识别。另一方面，只有ATF4、PNMA3和ZIK1与网络相互作用相关，更具体地涉及凋亡通路，且ATF4和PNMA3的差异表达仅在宫颈癌非干细胞中发生，并伴随ZIK1的存在。结论：我们提出，PNMA3的上调和ATF4的下调，特别是在宫颈癌非干细胞中，与ZIK1的上调以及凋亡和放化疗抵抗相关。因此，提示这些基因可能作为宫颈癌预后的潜在特征。
